# Accepted payment methods

Northstar Market accepts cards, approved bank transfers, and approved mobile-wallet payments. Cash on delivery is not available. A customer sees only payment methods supported for their order, address, and current checkout session. Payment acceptance does not mean that every payment has settled or that inventory has been reserved.

## Bank transfer review

An order paid by bank transfer remains pending until Northstar Market receives confirmation from its payment provider. A failed bank transfer does not reserve stock. Customers should not submit a second transfer until support confirms the first transfer cannot be matched, because duplicate payments require a separate reconciliation process. A payment screenshot is useful supporting information but is not by itself settlement confirmation.

## Card authorization and capture

A card authorization may appear before an order is dispatched. Northstar Market captures payment when the order is confirmed for fulfilment, subject to any bank-side controls. If a card authorization expires before capture, the customer may need to place a new order. Support should not describe an authorization hold as a completed refund.

## Checkout promotions

Only one checkout promotion code may be applied to an order. A promotion code cannot be combined with a wholesale price, staff price, or another promotion code unless the promotion itself explicitly says otherwise. Delivery offers are governed by the shipping policy, not by the existence of a promotion code. A failed promotion validation does not change item availability.

## Payment evidence boundaries

Payment data in this document explains checkout state but does not expose a customer's bank details, transaction history, or refund outcome. Support can use an order number and a provider confirmation to locate the correct process, but it must not accept a customer-provided screenshot as final evidence that funds settled. If a customer reports a duplicated transfer, the payment team must reconcile the transfers before an order is released or a refund is considered. A checkout confirmation page is not a guarantee that a bank transfer has cleared.

## Safe customer guidance

When a transfer is pending, the safe explanation is that the order waits for provider confirmation. When a card shows an authorization, the safe explanation is that it may be a temporary hold until capture or expiry. Neither situation should be described as a dispatch confirmation, a stock reservation, or a refund. Questions about delivery duration belong to the shipping policy, while eligibility for a completed-order refund belongs to the refund policy. Keeping those sources separate prevents an answer from inventing a combined rule that no approved document states.
